title: Contrastive learning
reading: A sparse content slide introducing contrastive learning. It poses the question of what to do when no predefined vocabulary (label set) is available, and answers that a vocabulary can be formed from the data itself — i.e., instances in the dataset serve as their own classes/targets, which is the core idea behind contrastive/self-supervised objectives. No further detail is given on the page.

concepts.name: Contrastive learning
concepts.why_it_matters: Self-supervised paradigm that learns representations by comparing examples rather than predicting fixed labels.

concepts.name: Vocabulary built from data itself
concepts.why_it_matters: Removes dependence on a hand-defined label set; each data instance acts as its own category.
